Agent contributions

  • Lead Codex agent — inspected Git, preserved the original one-shot instructions, established the objective, integrated each feature on development, owned transport and lifecycle integration, the API, live timeline, lineage, reset handling, seeded acceptance, final verification and this report. Reviewed and tested delegated work at each merge.
  • sphinx — identified the original UCL packet implementation and produced a Python 2 interoperability oracle. Ported Sphinx, implemented packet scheduling and replicated vaults, and built D3 geometry, lane overlays, transit markers and offline-processing corrections. Verified with wire fixtures, per-hop checks, transport regressions, layout tests and Chromium acceptance.
  • kademlia — researched and implemented original Kademlia RPCs, iterative lookups, record maintenance and recovery. Produced the HTML evidence generator, protocol inspectors and runtime intervention controls. Verified using simulated transport and lookup integration, offline bootstrap and slow-link tests, Svelte rendering and real browser interventions.
  • web — established the SvelteKit toolchain, contributed participant and traffic models, availability schedules and routing buckets. Built the real-browser test fixture and authored control, topology and 30-transmission acceptance coverage. Verified via unit suites, strict frontend checks, static build and Playwright.

Final acceptance and coverage

  • Final verification ran on development at b1a2ff5, the thirteenth non-fast-forward feature merge. Preflight started from main at 6b5001e and preserved the existing documentation at 7f9ded0. Commit d6647f2 added the active objective and evidence requirements to one-shot.md. The final evidence-only report commit follows the tested source revision.
  • Python 3.14.7: 144 tests passed in 6.95 seconds. Statement coverage for app and main was 95% (3,346 of 3,538 statements). Ruff found no lint errors, all 71 files met formatting rules and mypy reported no issues in 38 source files. One Starlette dependency warning concerns httpx in its test client.
  • Node 24.20.0 and npm 11.19.0: 25 Vitest tests passed. Unit coverage was 58.24% of statements, 51.99% of branches, 57.48% of functions and 60.28% of lines. Playwright exercises browser interaction separately from unit instrumentation. Svelte reported zero errors and zero warnings, ESLint and Prettier passed and the adapter-static production build succeeded.
  • Chromium: all eight end-to-end tests passed in 38.2 seconds. The timed full conversation took 34.8 seconds and the selected-receiver, node and boundary controls took 1.9 seconds. Geometry assertions covered 10 and 20 mixes, with live node identifiers, stage order, card overlap and peer selection.
  • The final handover also used independently launched Python and Vite processes on loopback ports 8000 and 5173. A separate real-browser acceptance run against these processes passed in 32.3 seconds and left the completed scenario available for inspection.
  • Seed 254 created Alice, Carol, David and Bob, four distinct Tor boundaries, 15 mixes, five DHT peers, five vaults and three conversations. Five exchanges per conversation produced 15 forward messages and 15 replies. All 30 messages were decrypted exactly once. The final clock was 20,399 logical ms with 27,600 sequenced events.
  • The operator edited Alice’s staged text, ran at an initial playback setting of 500 ms, changed pacing during execution to 12 ms and then 1 ms, blocked and restored a live path, paused an in-flight marker and re-enabled Bob’s polling after publication. Mix outages were 500 and 500,000 logical ms. Bob received nothing with polling disabled. The service recorded 24 failed path transits, six fresh packet retries, 30 manifest publications, 57 fragment retrievals and 441 safe lineage records.
  • Device receipts reconcile to 15 for Bob and five each for Alice, Carol and David. Tests checked actual source-route event paths, reply-lane markers, key learning after authenticated decryption and ciphertext identity across reconstruction. The clock stops at conversation completion, when unrelated cover or polling traffic can still be in flight.
  • The report embeds the full command output, including failed attempts and successful reruns. The downloadable .tar.xz archive preserves the original log bytes. Screenshots show the independent connection, topology and completed run.

Graphify index

  • The initial extraction used the local code-only Graphify installation after source became available. Subsequent source and schema checkpoints refreshed its local index. The final development update returned exit code 0 and reported no relevant changes. graphify-out/graph.json contains 1,374 nodes and 3,733 edges across 60 communities. The local Graphify configuration and generated outputs are excluded from Git.

Outstanding protocol decisions

  • Loopix 2017 and Kademlia 2002 are the selected algorithms. The local network carries logical datagrams, and each participant owns a Tor boundary. Tor circuits and the public networks are outside the model.
  • No externally maintained binding for the exact 2017 P-224 Sphinx forward-packet format was identified. The project maintains a pinned LGPL port of UCL sphinxmix 0.0.6, checked against an independent original Python 2 fixture. The egress adapter terminates the Sphinx packet and hands the opaque application body to storage. Replies use fresh packets and independently sample the same ordered layers.
  • The mailbox adapter issues seeded 160-bit lookup handles, making network decisions reproducible. The scenario seed can predict the handles. Lookup, polling, ciphertext length, placement and timing remain correlatable. A production mailbox privacy and discovery design remains open.
  • The encrypted manifest protects its message ID, chunk ordering, hashes and placement list. Vaults retain encrypted chunks, hashes and lengths. Replication requires one intact copy of each chunk. No erasure coding is implemented.
  • The receiving device learns an unverified reply public key after authenticated decryption. X25519, HKDF-SHA-256 and AES-256-GCM protect the application envelope. Sender authentication, forward secrecy, key rotation and real anonymity guarantees remain open.
  • Per-hop Sphinx replay tags protect the mix layer. The recipient deduplicates application message IDs. Keys and packet cryptography use operating-system entropy independently of the scenario seed.
  • The fixed polling interval defaults to 15,000 logical ms with three 256-byte padded response cells. An explicit intervention can suspend polling. The default topology uses three Loopix layers. The Kademlia cache lifetime decreases exponentially by proximity rank, with base two selected where the paper leaves the base open.
  • An inert GlobalObserver has an identity and lifecycle. The laboratory operator can schedule or impose outages and block paths, including deliberate in-flight loss. Configurable operator ownership supports correlated outages. Collusion, adversary inference and traffic-analysis resistance remain open.
